title: Braised Tofu
summary: Fry the tofu until golden, then braise it while spooning the sauce over. The frying step is the whole point.
intro:
Tofu falls apart in dubu-jorim when it goes straight into the braise without being fried. The surface has to cook firm before it can hold its shape in the sauce.

Blotting it dry with paper towel before frying is for the same reason. Water left on the tofu makes the oil spit and stops the outside from setting firm.
steps: Cut the tofu into 1.5 cm (1/2 in) slices and lay them on paper towel for 10 minutes to draw out the water. A light sprinkle of salt draws out more.
Mix all the sauce ingredients together.
Heat the cooking oil in a pan and fry the tofu over medium-high heat for 3 minutes on each side, until golden. Do not keep turning it.
Lay the fried tofu in the pan in a single layer and tuck the sliced onion in between the pieces.
Pour the sauce evenly over the top, cover, and braise over medium-low heat for 7 minutes.
Take the lid off and spoon the liquid from the pan over the tofu, over and over. This is how you work the seasoning in, rather than turning the pieces.
When about a third of the liquid is left, lay the diagonally sliced leek and green chilli on top and braise for 2 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and finish with the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Use a wide spatula rather than chopsticks to turn the tofu. Chopsticks tear it.
If you want a little meat in it, fry 50 g (1 3/4 oz) minced meat before you fry the tofu, then add it along with the sauce.
It keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheats well.
